summary: Learn AI-assisted evidence search, synthesis, and policy brief writing in 5 days. Build practical tools and apply them at work.
lede: AI for Research, Policy Analysis and Evidence Synthesis shows you how to apply AI across literature searching, screening, source appraisal, evidence extraction, and synthesis without handing over professional judgment. You will build structured workflows that connect search results to policy interpretation while preserving provenance, accountability, and methodological discipline. Through practical work with evidence matrices, screening logs, search strategies, synthesis notes, policy brief outlines, and decision tables, you will turn scattered AI use into a defensible process. The course helps you improve retrieval, manage repetitive tasks, and produce clearer policy-facing recommendations despite limited time, incomplete data, and uneven source quality.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who need to turn research and data into policy-ready evidence with AI-assisted workflows.
prerequisites: Participants should have working familiarity with policy analysis, research reading, or evidence-based reporting, plus comfort using spreadsheets and online databases. No coding is required for completion, although prior exposure to search operators, citation tools, or evidence review workflows will help you move faster. The course introduces AI-assisted searching and synthesis at an operational level, not software development or model building level, and uses examples that can be adapted to common institutional workflows.
topics: Generative AI at work & AI copilots
